So, for the last LATEX edition of 2026, we're holding mass for the unrepentant. Fallen angels, heretics, and anyone who's ever been told they're doing life wrong. Put on your Sunday best and come disappoint the Church (and your overtly pious aunt).
For the look, think sacrilegious glamour: religious imagery gone a little wrong, fetish takes on church wear, and relics that weirdly resemble your favourite sex toy. Basically, enough sin to get the whole congregation excommunicated.
We've cooked up a special roster for the occasion, bringing together some of our favourite local talents, LATEX residents, and Toronto's finest.
And yes, after popular demand, we're bringing back last edition's little ritual. Some traditions are worth keeping, apparently. Bring something to share with a stranger, and leave with an indelible memory.
Thank you, as always, for your trust and enthusiasm. All ticket tiers are pretty much SOLD OUT, with only LAST CALL tickets left. But if cost is a barrier, don't hesitate to reach out. We've got a 20% off promo code for LATEX regulars, friends & family, QTBIPOC folks, and nightlife workers. If you fall under any of these categories, consider this your personal invitation. We'd love to have you with us.
After everything this year has thrown at us, we'd love nothing more than to wrap it all up together, on the dancefloor, where we belong.
Confession is cancelled, and honestly, heaven's probably full of boring people anyway. Come worship at the wrong altar with us.
Latex is a temporary world. It does not exist by accident. It exists because we agree to protect and hold it carefully. Because we understand that freedom only works if everyone understands the weight of it. A ticket is intention, not entitlement. The door holds discretion. Capacity is limited and if the energy threatens the space, access can be refused or revoked. The organism defends itself.
Ground Rules
//DRESS CODE//
Dress with intention and interpret the theme as an offering to the room. Effort signals respect. Participation sustains the atmosphere.
Latex is a kink event and we simply do not want people showing up with just jeans and a T-shirt.
The outfit is absolutely mandatory and if you don't feel comfortable around kink, nudity or BDSM practices, LATEX might not be the appropriate event for you.
We strongly encourage kink wear // LATEX / PVC / LEATHER / CHAINS / LINGERIE etc...
If you have any doubts, feel free to contact us.
//CONSENT//
Consent is the architecture of this night. Nothing moves without it. Touch requires a clear yes. Dancing is not permission. Clothing is not permission. Chemistry is not permission. Silence is not permission. If someone pulls away, hesitates, or says no, that is the end of the exchange. This is a queer-centered space grounded in collective liberation. Liberation is not an aesthetic; it is a practice.
When meeting someone new, please ask for their pronouns! It doesn't feel nice to be misgendered.
Please make sure you approach the people you are interested in face to face, and not from the side or from behind.
Remember that people can change their minds or modify their consent at any time.
If you feel unwell or notice someone who might be, please inform the staff immediately. Care is not optional here. We look after one another.
We will have designated people you can go to in case anything happens. (Look for the pink armbands)
You are responsible for the attitude of the people you invite to our events and you can be held accountable for their misbehavior. Please choose wisely who you bring with you in order to keep LATEX a safe space for everyone.
//PERFORMERS//
Respect the performers and DJs. They are not props or décor. Do not touch performers unless clearly invited. Do not climb on stage. Do not cross into spaces that are not yours. What happens in the booth and on the stage is intentional. Honor the work.
Feel free to tip your favorite.
//THE NO NO NO's//
Keep your phones down. Use them only when necessary. Do not scroll in the heart of the dancefloor. No photography. No filming. Here, some of us move in freedom the outside world cannot touch. DO NOT TAKE THAT AWAY. Presence is more sacred than any record. Those who break this trust will be escorted out and barred from returning.
A designated professional photographer will be covering the event.
Harassment, coercion, predatory behavior, racism, transphobia, homophobia, misogyny, body shaming, or any form of discrimination ends your night immediately. No debate. No warning.
NO leering, creeping, following, or insisting.
*Definition of leering: looking or gazing in a lascivious or unpleasant way.
NO BYOB
NO smoking inside

Consent is mandatory.If it’s not an enthusiastic yes, it’s a no.
Negotiate before you play.
Discuss boundaries, limits, and safewords before starting any scene.
Do not interrupt a scene.Players must not be disturbed unless there is a safety concern.RED always means stop.
Immediately end the scene if RED is called.
Dungeon Monitors wearing pink armbands are here to help. If you feel unsafe, uncomfortable, or need assistance, reach out to them.

Watching is allowed, but give players space and never touch without explicit consent.
No intoxicated play.
If you are too intoxicated, you will not be allowed to participate in scenes.
Respect privacy.
What happens in the dungeon stays in the dungeon.
// RESPECT THE SPACE //
Use furniture and toys as intended.
Clean after yourself.
Sanitize equipment before and after use.
Share the space.
Do not monopolize furniture.
Be aware of your surroundings.
Ensure there is enough room to play safely.
Ask before joining a scene.
Never assume participation is welcome.
Do not remove dungeon equipment.
Furniture, toys, and gear belong to the dungeon.
Do not take, borrow without permission, or leave with them.

Respect, consent, and care guide everything here.
This is a space to explore safely. Dress for the vibe : latex, leather, fetish, or other expressive attire encouraged. Respect boundaries and look out for one another.
No phones. No photography. No filming.

Après une année sur la route qui a mené la maison de disques à Ibiza, Miami, LA, Amsterdam et New York, nous sommes heureux de revenir s’installer à la maison, dans notre Salon montréalais préféré.
On lance une nouvelle soirée mensuelle au Salon Daomé. Toute l’équipe de SLAPPED a grandi dans l’orbite du Salon, un pilier de la vie nocturne de notre ville. On a la chance de prolonger la nuit jusqu’à (au moins) 5 h du matin.
Pour cette soirée dite « d’industrie », on mélange les crowds et la musique pour trouver un nouveau groove.
On est ravis d’accueillir :
✧ RONCO ✧ animatrice radio, à la tête d’une maison de disques et cofondatrice de la série d’événements Fractus, qui fait du dancefloor une oasis depuis quatre ans.
✧ DUZA ✧ ce duo montréalais a sorti « Baby » avec nous en juin, sur notre compilation À Fleur de Son. Ils apportent de la classe à la deep tech montréalaise, autant derrière les platines qu’en studio, et on a hâte de les recevoir pour la première fois.
✧ NoKliché ✧ ces deux-là se sont rencontrés à Montréal et ont trouvé une alchimie artistique qui mélange les sons en une seule palette sonore. Ils ont sorti HI-FI, un album incroyable inspiré de leurs racines africaines et moyen-orientales, qui détourne le disco, le R&B et la lo-fi house pour en faire un vrai voyage sur le dancefloor.
Notre Label Boss, Mitch Oliver, jouera aussi en back-to-back avec notre A&R, Victor Rodriguez. Leur amitié s’est renforcée en devenant un partenariat. Ensemble, ils ont tissé le réseau dans lequel SLAPPED a pu grandir, et les voir côte à côte dans la cabine est peut-être notre expression la plus vraie.
Autant dire que les tracks vont SLAPPER. On se voit au Salon, pour ce qu’on espère être la première d’une longue série.

22 h 30 à 5 h

4465, boul. Saint-Laurent

After a year on the road that brought the label to Ibiza, Miami, LA, Amsterdam, and New York, we’re happy to be settling back home in our beloved Montreal.
Kicking off a new club night at a true Montreal gem, Le Salon Daomé. The whole SLAPPED team grew into their own in the orbit of Salon, a club cornerstone of our city. We have the opportunity to stretch the night out until (at least) 5am for an extended gathering around the music.
For this night, we reached out to our community to build new bridges, connect new sounds and settle into a new groove.
We’re stoked to be joined by:
**✧** RONCO **✧** radio host, label runner, and cofounder of the Fractus event series which has been making the dancefloor an oasis for the last four years.
**✧** DUZA **✧** this Montreal duo released “Baby” with us on our À Fleur de Son VA in June. They bring class to Montreal deep tech both in the booth & in the studio & we can’t wait to have them on for the first time.
**✧** NoKliché **✧** these two met in Montreal and found an artistic alchemy that blends all kinds of sounds into a unified palette. They dropped an unreal LP, HI-FI, drawing inspiration from their African and Middle Eastern roots, subverting the sounds of disco, rnb and lofi house into a proper dancefloor journey.
We’ll also have our label head Mitch Oliver going back to back with our A&R, Victor Rodriguez. A friendship bolstered by partnership, the two together have woven the web for SLAPPED to grow in, and having them together in the booth is perhaps our truest expression.
Safe to say we can expect tracks that SLAP. See you at Salon for hopefully the first of many.

Classically trained violist Geneviève Heistek has been an active contributor to
Montreal’s independent music community for over 25 years, working across rock,
jazz, and experimental genres.
Heistek is best known for her work in Hanged Up, an avant-folk-metal duo formed
with drummer Eric Craven. The project released three albums on Constellation
Records, including Transit of Venus (2012)—a collaboration with minimalist
pioneer Tony Conrad that was named one of SPIN Magazine’s top 10 avant-garde
records of that year.
Her collaborative history includes co-founding the post-folk group Sackville,
the Mile End Ladies’ String Auxiliary (MELSA), and the ambient post-rock
collective Set Fire to Flames. She has performed alongside artists such as
violinist Warren Ellis and Patti Smith, and contributed improvisational work to
the soundtrack of the Oscar-nominated NFB film Madame Tutli-Putli. She has
toured extensively, and performed at international festivals including Roskilde,
All Tomorrow’s Parties, and the Festival International de Musique Actuelle de
Victoriaville.
Currently, Heistek is a long-standing member of Sam Shalabi’s avant-Egyptian big
band, Land of Kush, appearing on multiple releases including The Big Mango and
Sand Enigma. Recent projects include performing alongside Shalabi and composer
